items.title: 52157_Count Basie oral history interview
items.q: Of course, we weren't lucky enough to have Mary Lou there. Mary Lou Williams.

ctx.x: Were there any Kansas City musicians who, you know, are not big names, but are still working there? Or were there any people you know, who wouldn't be famous, let's say.

They're kind of famous around that area. You know, like (inaudible), for many years, he was one of the top guys. Baby Lovett and oh, so many of them gone that was there, you know, but can't name too many now. That are there now. Of course, we weren't lucky enough to have Mary Lou there. Mary Lou Williams.

items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: They could swing like Count Basie. It was just like Count Basie started the beat that he had... the approach of Count Basie was without slapstick

ctx.x: rhythm section first." And after that the trumpets and the saxophones. In this particular band they had a guy that played - they called him like a clown. He did all the acrobatics and everything on his back with this tenor and all that. They had other musicians that were real true musicians and what I did when I began writing, I'd teach this guy how to phrase with them because he was a little corny - the one that was doing all the tricks while he was playing. They did little acts and they did everything. They…
They worked a lot of white dates?
